newsitem.title: USA: World Bank to approve $1.7 billion in Russia loans. [CORRECTED 03:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: World Bank to approve $1.7 billion in Russia loans. [CORRECTED 03:23 GMT]

text.p: The World Bank is expected to approve nearly $1.7 billion in loans for Russia this month to help it transform its economy and deal with the at times painful fall-out from its reforms, officials said on Monday.
The loans will range from $22.6 (corrects from $26.2) million to improve government analysis of the economy to an $800 million credit to strengthen the country's social safety net, they said.
Negotiations on the jumbo $800 million credit, the Bank's biggest ever for Russia, were completed over the weekend.

The loan will be used to reshape Russia's social protection programs to help the poor and other vulnerable groups cope with fall-out from Russia's reforms. Key areas covered by the loan will be pensions, unemployment assistance, and welfare, including maternity and sick leave.
Bank officials said the lending agency's board is expected to consider the credit on June 26.

The other loans are expected to be taken up by the Bank's Board on Thursday. Aside from the $22.6 million (corrects from $26.2) million credit for government economic analysis, this package is comprised of:
-- $600 million for wide-ranging structural reforms throughout the economy;
-- $71 million to improve higher education through enhanced teaching methods, reduced class sizes, more and better textbooks and other measures;
-- $40 million to reform the problem-plagued power sector;
-- $66 million for health care reform, including improved out-patient care; and
-- $85 million to help privatized companies restructure.

World Bank President James Wolfensohn said in April that the lending agency could lend Russia $3 billion a year over the next two years, mainly in projects dealing with the painful social consequences of economic reform.
"Our objective is to move ... into lending which is related to structural reform and investment programs," he told a news conference in Moscow.
